title: Cross-func roadmap alignment — 1:1 prep (Product / Eng / Applied ML)
content:
Purpose:
Quick 1:1 prep notes before the cross-functional roadmap sync between Product (Mina), Eng (Lucas) and Applied ML (Ava). Objective: surface hard constraints and open tradeoffs so the broader sync can land on a clear rollout plan and owners for the next 90 days.

Meeting logistics:
- Date: 2026-04-12 10:00am PT (pre-brief at 9:40am for 15m)
- Attendees: Mina (Product), Lucas (Eng), Ava (Applied ML), me (Jasper)
- Duration: 45m
- Pre-reads: Q2 roadmap draft (Confluence), latency SLO baseline (ENG-5421), model-onboarding checklist PR#378

Sharable objectives (two-line):
1) Agree on minimum viable rollout for dynamic batching + KV cache across hosted API and dedicated pools (target: safe canary by end of May).
2) Decide whether to prioritize 8-bit quantization profile for Llama-externals or defer to Q3 after more evals.

Agenda (proposed):
1) Quick sync on constraints (5m): infra, infra budget, hiring gaps
2) E2E plan overview (10m): Product sketches what success looks like + persona impacts
3) Engineering feasibility (12m): Lucas on infra effort and risky dependencies
4) Applied ML (10m): Ava on eval results, quality delta, and suggested fallback policies
5) Decisions & actions (8m): owners, duedates, followups

Key prep notes / talking points:
- Infra capacity: Dedicated pool capacity is ~60% committed in west-1 for Q2; any burst will need cross-region support or scaled-down batch window. Lucas to confirm exact GPU hour cushion before the meeting.
- Latency SLOs: Product wants p95 < 180ms for short-chat tier; current serving runtime baseline p95 is ~220ms with default batching. Need to discuss aggressive prefetch+cache for hot prefixes.
- Cost tradeoff: Quantization to 8-bit reduces token cost ~28% in perf sims but shows a small accuracy degradation on our rerank evals (Ava will show examples). Decision hinge: are customer-facing regressions acceptable for beta?
- Rollout policy: propose staged rollout: internal -> dedicated customers opt-in -> hosted default with opt-out window. Tools needed: per-customer config flag + monitoring alert thresholds.
- Eval coverage gap: current prompt set lacks multi-turn retrieval examples. Ava to add 40 prompts that exercise retrieval + long context by EOD 4/15.

Open questions to surface:
- If we accept 8-bit by default, what rollback window do we require? (1 day? 3 days?)
- Can Dedicated customers pin older model variants without costing us disproportionate infra? Need input from billing/product.
- Who will own the “quality regression” playbook (alerts -> human triage -> rollback)? Suggest SRE + Applied ML + Product on-call rotation.

Risks called out:
- Latency regressions under multiplexed traffic patterns if batching heuristics overshoot. Mitigation: per-route batching caps, early abort.
- Customer trust risk if we flip defaults without clear opt-out. Mitigation: communications + rollout notes in Console.

Concrete action items (owner / due):
1) Lucas: confirm west-1 dedicated GPU cushion (exact GPU-hours) and ETA for per-route batching caps — due 2026-04-14.
2) Ava: augment eval set with 40 multi-turn retrieval prompts; produce summary table comparing baseline/8-bit/quantized-llma by 2026-04-15.
3) Mina: draft customer-facing rollout plan + opt-in/opt-out language for Console banners; initial draft 2026-04-16.
4) Jasper (me): draft short decision memo for execs summarizing recommended path + rollback window options — 2026-04-16.
5) Team: schedule a 30m follow-up checkpoint (post-rollout) for one week after canary starts — owner: Mina; to be scheduled during main sync.

Notes to self (Jasper):
- Raise the possibility of an A/B fallback that routes high-risk customers to a conservative variant automatically.
- Keep the language in the canary announcement explicit about what metrics we watch (p95 latency, error rate, quality score delta).
- Be ready with two rollback windows: 24h aggressive (must have manual rollback steps ready), 72h conservative (auto revert if quality delta > threshold).

Pre-meeting checklist (things to have ready):
- Lucas: a slide with infra constraints + short list of blockers (1 slide)
- Ava: 1-2 failure-case prompts to demo quality regression live (keep it short)
- Mina: list of top 5 customers likely to opt-in for Dedicated canary

Post-meeting follow-up template (for minutes):
- Decisions made
- Owners and due dates (copy into Jira)
- Risks & mitigations agreed
- Communication plan and next checkpoint

Quick links referenced: 
- Roadmap: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROADMAP-2026-Q2
- Latency baseline: ENG-5421
- Model onboarding PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/378

Unresolved items to push to group sync if not decided in 1:1:
- Default rollback window length
- Exact threshold for auto-revert based on quality delta

End of prep notes. Keep this short during the actual 1:1; use the pre-brief to put the hard constraints on the table first.

---
Scratch/brainstorm snippets (not for meeting):
- Could offer a ‘reduced-cost beta’ tag: customers running on quantized models get a billing discount and early-access terms. Helps mitigate trust risk.
- Small experiment: enable 8-bit for non-retrieval flows first, that would reduce regression surface.
